findings.problem: The U5-R7 fix (73aeec5) makes a hold inactive whenever now() < hold.setAt, so ANY backward clock step, even 1 ms, cancels an active rate-limit or transient hold and lets a refresh request out while GitHub is still rate-limiting (E-15 l.36: do not retry until retry-after has elapsed; pre-mortem 4; L-13 by the spec's own 6.5 definition, where a hold is active while now() < until). Before R7 a backward step stretched the hold (safe, too long); after R7 it drops it (one request per step, then a new hold). Small backward steps are the common ones (NTP/Windows Time corrections after resume), so this trades a latency defect for a request during a rate limit. Each further step buys one more request: five 1 ms steps gave five refresh requests against a 429 with retry-after 120.

findings.fix: Re-anchor instead of dropping: in holdActive(), `if (t < hold.setAt) { hold.until = t + (hold.until - hold.setAt); hold.setAt = t; } return t < hold.until;` (the hold restarts in the new time, never stretched by the step and never cancelled by it), or anchor holds on a monotonic source. Adjust refresh test 15 accordingly: after the day-back step renewalHeld stays true for the hold's length (30 s), a read inside it sends the token the clock calls valid once (GS-4), and the skew rule refreshes once the hold ends; keep P1/P1b/P1c as pins (backward steps of 1 ms, 1 s and 5 s during a 429 hold and a 30 s hold send no refresh). Record the mutation proof (holdActive without the re-anchor: P1 red) and tell the lead the 6.5 formula and the 6.8 'clock steps back' row need the As-built note updated.

findings.problem: A refresh answer about the old account that lands inside the sign-in commit's replace step 7 (after the store set `live = next` at step 6, before commitPoint runs generation++ and renewAccountChanged) still goes through failed()/sameOrFail(): the U5-R10 guard checks only the generation, which has not moved yet, so the waiter rejects with GITHUB_RENEWAL_UNAVAILABLE although a new signed-in account is live and could serve it; the hold it sets is wiped a moment later by commitPoint. Narrow window (the old refs' tombstone+remove+file write), latency only, no token at risk; the spec's 6.3/6.5 order has the same window.
